Bayesian nonparametric inference for kinetic interacting particle systems: numerical experiments¶

Companion notebook to the paper Bayesian nonparametric inference for kinetic interacting particle systems. All numerical experiments of Section 3 of the paper are reproduced here, under its section numbering; analyses that support the text without a figure of their own appear under unnumbered headings. Every figure of the paper is written to fig/ as a vector PDF, under the file name used by the LaTeX source, drawn at its printed size and in the fonts and notation of the paper.

Luca Martucci, 2026.

3.1 A Hermite–Fourier spectral discretisation of the Vlasov–Fokker–Planck equation¶

Setup and figure style, the phase-space grid and the Maxwellian-adapted Hermite basis, and the coefficient-hierarchy solver with Strang splitting.

def paper_figure(frac, height, **kw):
    """Figure of width frac*TEXTWIDTH and the given height (inches), laid out at its printed size;
    the paper includes it at width frac*\\textwidth, that is, unscaled."""
    return plt.subplots(figsize=(frac*TEXTWIDTH, height), layout="constrained", **kw)

def save_figure(fig, name):
    """Write fig/<name>.pdf (vector graphics; heatmaps embedded at 600 dpi) and display it."""
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG_DIR, f"{name}.pdf"))
    plt.show()

def set_q_axis(ax, label=True):
    """Position axis on the torus T = R/2πZ ≃ [0, 2π)."""
    ax.set_xlim(0, 2*np.pi)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(5)*np.pi/2, ["$0$", r"$\pi/2$", r"$\pi$", r"$3\pi/2$", r"$2\pi$"])
    if label:
        ax.set_xlabel("$q$")

def heatmap(ax, Z, x, y, cmap, label, **kw):
    """Field Z[i, j] at the points (x[j], y[i]) of uniform grids, with a labelled colour bar."""
    dx, dy = x[1]-x[0], y[1]-y[0]
    im = ax.imshow(Z, origin='lower', aspect='auto', cmap=cmap, interpolation='bilinear',
                   extent=[x[0]-dx/2, x[-1]+dx/2, y[0]-dy/2, y[-1]+dy/2], **kw)
    cb = ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax, pad=0.02, aspect=25)
    cb.set_label(label); cb.outline.set_linewidth(0.6)
    cb.ax.tick_params(width=0.6, length=2.5)
    ax.set_ylim(y[0], y[-1])
    return im

# ---- quadrature and interpolation on the periodic grid ----------------------------------------
# On the grid q_j = j*dq of T the rectangle rule is the quadrature of the torus, exact for
# trigonometric polynomials of degree < Nq/2 (a trapezoidal rule on q_0,...,q_{Nq-1} would omit the
# closing interval [q_{Nq-1}, 2π]); momentum integrals over a finite window use the trapezoidal rule.
trapezoid = getattr(np, "trapezoid", None) or np.trapz      # np.trapz was renamed in NumPy 2.0

def torus_integral(g, dq, axis=-1):
    return np.sum(g, axis=axis)*dq

def cosine_coefficients(W, q, K):
    """Cosine coefficients a_k = (1/π) ∫_T W(q) cos(kq) dq, k = 1, ..., K, of grid values W."""
    dq = q[1] - q[0]
    a = np.array([torus_integral(W*np.cos(kk*q), dq)/np.pi for kk in range(1, K+1)])
    return np.round(a, 13) + 0.0          # rounding off the floating-point noise of exact zeros

def trig_interp(values, x, axis=-1):
    """Trigonometric interpolant of values on the grid q_j = 2πj/Nq, evaluated at the points x
    (to draw the pseudo-spectral solutions smoothly)."""
    v = np.moveaxis(np.asarray(values, dtype=float), axis, -1)
    Nq = v.shape[-1]
    E = np.exp(1j*np.outer(np.fft.fftfreq(Nq, d=1/Nq), x))
    if Nq % 2 == 0:
        E[Nq//2] = np.cos(Nq//2*x)                          # symmetric Nyquist term
    return np.moveaxis(np.real((np.fft.fft(v, axis=-1)/Nq) @ E), -1, axis)

q_fine = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 401)                       # plotting grid on [0, 2π]

def plot_coefficients(ax, mean, sd, truth, loc='best'):
    """Posterior mean ± one standard deviation of the cosine coefficients, against the truth."""
    pos = np.arange(1, len(mean)+1)
    ax.errorbar(pos, mean, yerr=sd, fmt='o', ms=3.5, capsize=2.5, elinewidth=1,
                label=r'posterior mean $\pm$ s.d.')
    ax.plot(pos, truth, 'rx', ms=6, mew=1.4, label='truth')
    ax.axhline(0, color='k', lw=0.4)
    ax.set_xticks(pos, [f"$a_{{{m}}}$" for m in pos])
    handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
    ax.legend(handles[::-1], labels[::-1], loc=loc)          # posterior first, then the truth

def plot_trace(ax, ll, burn, N, ylabel):
    """Log-likelihood trace with the burn-in and the plateau -N/2 marked."""
    ax.plot(ll, lw=0.5, color='C0')
    ax.axvline(burn, color='C3', ls=':', lw=1.2, label='burn-in')
    ax.axhline(-N/2, color='C2', ls='--', lw=1, label=r'$-N/2$')
    lo, hi = ll.min(), max(ll.max(), -N/2)
    pad = 0.06*(hi - lo)
    ax.set_ylim(lo - pad, hi + pad)
    ax.set_xlabel("iteration"); ax.set_ylabel(ylabel); ax.legend(loc='lower right')

def gauss(x, m, sd):
    return np.exp(-0.5*((x-m)/sd)**2)/(sd*np.sqrt(2*np.pi))

def plot_marginals(prior_sd, post_mean, post_sd, truth, shrink, label='posterior', name=None):
    """Prior (filled) against Laplace posterior marginals of a_1, ..., a_12, with the truth
    (dashed) and the posterior shrinkage S_k in each panel title."""
    fig, axes = paper_figure(0.95, 3.5, nrows=3, ncols=4)
    for m, ax in enumerate(axes.ravel()):
        lim = 3*prior_sd[m]
        xg = np.concatenate([np.linspace(-lim, lim, 801), post_mean[m] + np.linspace(-6, 6, 801)*post_sd[m]])
        xg = np.sort(xg[np.abs(xg) <= lim])
        ax.fill_between(xg, gauss(xg, 0, prior_sd[m]), color='C3', alpha=0.30, lw=0, label='prior')
        ax.plot(xg, gauss(xg, post_mean[m], post_sd[m]), color='C3', lw=1.3, label=label)
        ax.axvline(truth[m], color='k', ls='--', lw=0.9, label='truth')
        ax.set_xlim(-lim, lim); ax.set_ylim(bottom=0); ax.set_yticks([])
        ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(nbins=4, symmetric=True))
        ax.set_title(rf"$a_{{{m+1}}}$,  $\mathscr{{S}}_{{{m+1}}}={shrink[m]:.2f}$", fontsize=8)
        if m == 0:
            ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper right', handlelength=1.4)
    if name:
        save_figure(fig, name)
    else:
        plt.show()

def make_grid(Nq, L=2*np.pi):
    q  = np.arange(Nq) * (L / Nq)
    dq = L / Nq
    k  = 2*np.pi * np.fft.fftfreq(Nq, d=dq)
    return q, dq, k

def hermite_eval(NH, p, beta):
    # B[i, n] = e_n(p_i) = sqrt(beta)/sqrt(2 pi n!) He_n(sqrt(beta) p) exp(-beta p^2 / 2)
    xi    = np.sqrt(beta) * np.atleast_1d(p)
    gauss = np.sqrt(beta) / np.sqrt(2*np.pi) * np.exp(-0.5*xi**2)
    B = np.zeros((len(xi), NH))
    for n in range(NH):
        c = np.zeros(n+1); c[n] = 1.0
        B[:, n] = hermeval(xi, c) / np.sqrt(float(math.factorial(n))) * gauss
    return B

# quick checks of the two defining properties of e_n

B = hermite_eval(6, pp, beta_chk)
ints = trapezoid(B, pp, axis=0)                 # should be (1,0,0,0,0,0)
print("int e_n dp      =", np.round(ints, 4))
print("max |e_0 - M|   =", np.max(np.abs(B[:,0] -
      np.sqrt(beta_chk/(2*np.pi))*np.exp(-0.5*beta_chk*pp**2))))

def build_linear_exponentials(k, NH, gamma, beta, dt):
    Ehalf = np.empty((len(k), NH, NH), dtype=complex)
    Efull = np.empty((len(k), NH, NH), dtype=complex)
    n = np.arange(NH)
    for ik, kk in enumerate(k):
        L = np.zeros((NH, NH), dtype=complex)
        L[n, n] = -gamma * n                                  # friction (diagonal)
        for m in range(NH):                                   # streaming (tridiagonal)
            if m-1 >= 0:  L[m, m-1] += -(1j*kk/np.sqrt(beta)) * np.sqrt(m)
            if m+1 < NH:  L[m, m+1] += -(1j*kk/np.sqrt(beta)) * np.sqrt(m+1)
        Ehalf[ik] = expm(0.5*dt*L)
        Efull[ik] = expm(dt*L)
    return Ehalf, Efull

def force_kick(c, A, tau, beta):
    # exact exponential of the nilpotent force generator (N c)_n = sqrt(beta n) A c_{n-1}
    NH = c.shape[0]
    sb  = np.sqrt(beta * np.arange(NH))
    out, term = c.copy(), c.copy()
    for j in range(1, NH):                                    # nilpotent => finite sum
        new = np.zeros_like(term)
        new[1:] = sb[1:, None] * A[None, :] * term[:-1]
        term = new * (tau / j)
        out += term
        if not np.any(term): break
    return out

class KineticVFP:
    def __init__(self, q, dq, k, NH, gamma, beta, dt, V):
        self.q, self.dq, self.k = q, dq, k
        self.NH, self.gamma, self.beta, self.dt = NH, gamma, beta, dt
        self.dV = np.real(np.fft.ifft(1j*k*np.fft.fft(V)))                # dV/dq
        self.Ehalf, self.Efull = build_linear_exponentials(k, NH, gamma, beta, dt)

    def force_field(self, rho, W):
        Wconv_hat = self.dq * np.fft.fft(W) * np.fft.fft(rho)            # W * rho
        dWconv    = np.real(np.fft.ifft(1j*self.k*Wconv_hat))
        return -self.dV - dWconv                                          # A = -d/dq (V + W*rho)

    def linear_step(self, c, E):
        chat = np.fft.fft(c, axis=1)                                      # (NH, Nq)
        chat = np.einsum('kmn,nk->mk', E, chat)                           # apply E_k per wavenumber
        return np.real(np.fft.ifft(chat, axis=1))

    def step(self, c, W):
        dt = self.dt
        c = force_kick(c, self.force_field(c[0], W), dt/2, self.beta)
        c = self.linear_step(c, self.Efull)
        c = force_kick(c, self.force_field(c[0], W), dt/2, self.beta)
        return c

    def solve(self, W, c_init, Nt, save_every=1):
        c = c_init.copy()
        saved, times = [c.copy()], [0.0]
        for nstep in range(Nt):
            c = self.step(c, W)
            if (nstep+1) % save_every == 0:
                saved.append(c.copy()); times.append((nstep+1)*self.dt)
        return np.array(times), np.array(saved)        # saved: (Ns, NH, Nq)

3.1.4 Validation of the solver¶

Four independent checks: (1) exact friction spectrum, (2)–(3) mass conservation, equilibrium stationarity and $O(\Delta t^2)$ consistency, and (4) an independent interacting-particle cross-check.

In [4]:
# (1) friction eigenstructure: c_n(t) = exp(-gamma n t) c_n(0)
Nq, NH = 48, 14
gamma, beta = 1.0, 1.0
q, dq, k = make_grid(Nq)
solver0 = KineticVFP(q, dq, k, NH, gamma, beta, dt=0.05, V=np.zeros(Nq))
c0 = np.zeros((NH, Nq))
c0[0], c0[1], c0[2], c0[3] = 1/(2*np.pi), 0.3/(2*np.pi), 0.2/(2*np.pi), 0.1/(2*np.pi)
times, sol = solver0.solve(np.zeros(Nq), c0, Nt=20, save_every=2)
print("Friction relaxation (uniform in q):")
for n in [1, 2, 3]:
    num   = sol[:, n, :].mean(axis=1) * 2*np.pi
    exact = c0[n, 0] * 2*np.pi * np.exp(-gamma*n*times)
    print(f"  mode n={n}: max rel. error vs exp(-{n}t) = "
          f"{np.max(np.abs(num-exact)/np.abs(exact+1e-15)):.2e}")

# (2)+(3) mass conservation, equilibrium stationarity, O(dt^2)
V  = -np.cos(q)
W  = -np.cos(q) + 0.5*np.cos(2*q)

# self-consistent McKean-Vlasov equilibrium density via Picard iteration
rho = np.ones(Nq) / (2*np.pi)
for _ in range(500):
    Wconv = np.real(np.fft.ifft(dq*np.fft.fft(W)*np.fft.fft(rho)))
    new   = np.exp(-beta*(V + Wconv)); new /= new.sum()*dq
    if np.max(np.abs(new-rho)) < 1e-14: break
    rho = new
c_eq = np.zeros((NH, Nq)); c_eq[0] = rho

solver = KineticVFP(q, dq, k, NH, gamma, beta, dt=0.02, V=V)
rho0 = 1 + 0.6*np.sin(q) + 0.3*np.cos(2*q); rho0 = np.clip(rho0, 1e-3, None); rho0 /= rho0.sum()*dq
c_init = np.zeros((NH, Nq)); c_init[0] = rho0
times, sol = solver.solve(W, c_init, Nt=100, save_every=10)
print("Mass over time:", np.round(sol[:, 0, :].sum(axis=1)*dq, 12))

print("\nEquilibrium drift vs dt (Strang 2nd order):")
for dt in [0.08, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01]:
    s = KineticVFP(q, dq, k, NH, gamma, beta, dt, V)
    _, traj = s.solve(W, c_eq, Nt=int(1.6/dt), save_every=10)
    print(f"  dt={dt:.3f}  max|c(t)-c_eq| = {np.max(np.abs(traj-c_eq[None])):.3e}")

# (4) independent particle (IPS) cross-check, up to the horizon T = 2
dt = 0.01
solver = KineticVFP(q, dq, k, NH, gamma, beta, dt, V)
T = 2.0; Nt = int(round(T/dt))
_, sol = solver.solve(W, c_init, Nt, save_every=Nt)
rho_pde = sol[-1, 0, :]

# Histogram bins centred at the grid points, [q_j - dq/2, q_j + dq/2): the value of bin j estimates
# the density at q_j, where the convolution is evaluated and the spectral density is compared, and
# each particle feels the mean-field force at its nearest grid point.
def grid_bin(x):
    return np.floor(((x + dq/2) % (2*np.pi))/dq).astype(int) % Nq

def histogram_density(x):
    return np.bincount(grid_bin(x), minlength=Nq)/(len(x)*dq)

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
n_part = 200_000
cdf = np.cumsum(rho0*dq); cdf /= cdf[-1]
qj = np.interp(rng.random(n_part), cdf, q)        # q0 ~ rho0
pj = rng.standard_normal(n_part) / np.sqrt(beta)  # p0 ~ Maxwellian
W_hat = np.fft.fft(W)
for _ in range(Nt):
    hist    = histogram_density(qj)
    dWconv  = np.real(np.fft.ifft(1j*k*dq*W_hat*np.fft.fft(hist)))
    force   = -np.sin(qj) - dWconv[grid_bin(qj)]  # -dV - d(W*rho),  V=-cos
    pj += dt*force - gamma*pj*dt + np.sqrt(2*gamma/beta*dt)*rng.standard_normal(n_part)
    qj  = (qj + pj*dt) % (2*np.pi)
hist_T = histogram_density(qj)
errL2  = np.sqrt(torus_integral((hist_T - rho_pde)**2, dq))
print(f"||rho_hist(T) - rho_PDE(T)||_L2 = {errL2:.4f}   (density scale 1/(2 pi) = {1/(2*np.pi):.3f}; "
      f"root-mean-square relative discrepancy {np.sqrt(np.mean((hist_T - rho_pde)**2))*2*np.pi:.1%})")

fig, ax = paper_figure(0.62, 2.0)
ax.plot(q_fine, trig_interp(rho0, q_fine), 'k:', lw=1.2, label=r'$\rho_0$')
ax.plot(q_fine, trig_interp(rho_pde, q_fine), color='C0', lw=1.4, label=r'$\rho^{\mathrm{PDE}}(T)$')
ax.plot(q, hist_T, 'o', color='C3', ms=3, label=r'$\rho^{\mathrm{hist}}(T)$')
set_q_axis(ax); ax.legend()
save_figure(fig, "ips_crosscheck")

3.1.5 Hypocoercivity in the discretised generator¶

# Spectrum of the linear streaming+friction operator L_k, wavenumber by wavenumber.
NH_spec, gamma_spec, beta_spec = 14, 1.0, 1.0

def Lk_matrix(kk, NH, gamma, beta):
    L = np.zeros((NH, NH), dtype=complex)
    for m in range(NH):
        L[m, m] = -gamma * m                                       # friction (diagonal)
        if m-1 >= 0:  L[m, m-1] += -(1j*kk/np.sqrt(beta)) * np.sqrt(m)     # streaming
        if m+1 < NH:  L[m, m+1] += -(1j*kk/np.sqrt(beta)) * np.sqrt(m+1)
    return L

k_scan = np.arange(0, 9)
slowest = np.array([np.linalg.eigvals(Lk_matrix(kk, NH_spec, gamma_spec, beta_spec)).real.max()
                    for kk in k_scan])
print("k             :", k_scan)
print("max_j Re mu_j :", np.round(slowest, 3))
print(f"\nhypocoercive gap opened by streaming: {0.0:.2f} at k=0  ->  {-slowest[1]:.2f} at k=1")

# least-damped relaxation rate against the wavenumber
fig, ax = paper_figure(0.48, 2.1)
ax.plot(k_scan, -slowest, 'o-', color='C0', ms=3.5)
ax.axhline(0, color='k', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(k_scan)
ax.set_xlabel("wavenumber $k$"); ax.set_ylabel(r"$-\mathrm{max}_j\,\operatorname{Re}\,\mu_j$")
save_figure(fig, "gap_vs_k")

# eigenvalues mu of the truncated L_k in the complex plane at a few wavenumbers
fig, ax = paper_figure(0.48, 2.1)
for kk, col in zip([0, 1, 3, 6], ['C3', 'C0', 'C2', 'C1']):
    ev = np.linalg.eigvals(Lk_matrix(kk, NH_spec, gamma_spec, beta_spec))
    ax.scatter(ev.real, ev.imag, s=9, color=col, label=f"$k={kk}$", zorder=3, linewidths=0)
ax.axvline(0, color='k', lw=0.5)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(integer=True))
ax.set_xlabel(r"$\operatorname{Re}\,\mu$"); ax.set_ylabel(r"$\operatorname{Im}\,\mu$")
ax.legend()
save_figure(fig, "Lk_spectrum")

3.2 Synthetic data and the discrete measurement models¶

Ground truth $W_0$, the initial state $\phi=\rho_0\otimes M_\beta$, and the discrete observation designs (data generated at a finer resolution to avoid the inverse crime).

In [8]:
def generate_data(seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    Nq, NH_hi, gamma, beta = 48, 20, 1.0, 1.0
    T, dt_hi = 2.0, 0.01
    q, dq, k = make_grid(Nq)
    V = -np.cos(q)

    W_true = -np.cos(q) + 0.5*np.cos(2*q) - 0.25*np.cos(3*q)
    rho0   = 1 + 0.6*np.sin(q) + 0.3*np.cos(2*q)
    rho0   = np.clip(rho0, 1e-3, None); rho0 /= rho0.sum()*dq
    c_init = np.zeros((NH_hi, Nq)); c_init[0] = rho0

    solver_hi = KineticVFP(q, dq, k, NH_hi, gamma, beta, dt_hi, V)
    times, sol = solver_hi.solve(W_true, c_init, Nt=int(T/dt_hi), save_every=2)  # snapshots @ 0.02

    N_obs, sigma = 3000, 0.004
    pmax = 3.5 / np.sqrt(beta)
    t_idx = rng.integers(1, len(times), N_obs)       # exclude t=0
    q_idx = rng.integers(0, Nq, N_obs)
    p_obs = rng.uniform(-pmax, pmax, N_obs)
    B = hermite_eval(NH_hi, p_obs, beta)
    f_clean = np.einsum('in,in->i', sol[t_idx, :, q_idx], B)
    Y = f_clean + sigma*rng.standard_normal(N_obs)

    return dict(q=q, dq=dq, k=k, T=T, gamma=gamma, beta=beta, V=V, rho0=rho0,
                W_true=W_true, times=times, sol_hi=sol, c_init=c_init,
                t_idx=t_idx, q_idx=q_idx, p_obs=p_obs, Y=Y, sigma=sigma, f_clean=f_clean)

data = generate_data(0)
print(f"snapshots={len(data['times'])} (dt=0.02 to T={data['T']}),  "
      f"N_obs={len(data['Y'])},  sigma={data['sigma']}")
print(f"f range = [{data['f_clean'].min():.3f}, {data['f_clean'].max():.3f}],  "
      f"noise/signal ~ {data['sigma']/data['f_clean'].std():.2f}")
print(f"mass t=0: {data['sol_hi'][0,0].sum()*data['dq']:.10f}   "
      f"mass t=T: {data['sol_hi'][-1,0].sum()*data['dq']:.10f}")

snapshots=101 (dt=0.02 to T=2.0),  N_obs=3000,  sigma=0.004
f range = [0.000, 0.113],  noise/signal ~ 0.15
mass t=0: 1.0000000000   mass t=T: 1.0000000000

3.3 Empirical forward stability¶

In [10]:
inf_kw = dict(NH=14, dt=0.02)                      # inference-resolution solver
solver = KineticVFP(data['q'], data['dq'], data['k'], inf_kw['NH'],
                    data['gamma'], data['beta'], inf_kw['dt'], data['V'])
c_init_inf = np.zeros((inf_kw['NH'], len(q))); c_init_inf[0] = data['rho0']
Nt_inf = int(data['T']/inf_kw['dt'])
Bp_inf = hermite_eval(inf_kw['NH'], P, data['beta'])

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
_, base = solver.solve(data['W_true'], c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=Nt_inf)
fbase = base[-1].T @ Bp_inf.T

eps_list = np.array([1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2, 1e-1, 3e-1]); errs = []
for eps in eps_list:
    dW = sum(eps*rng.standard_normal()/m**2*np.cos(m*q) for m in range(1, 6))
    _, pert = solver.solve(data['W_true']+dW, c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=Nt_inf)
    fp = pert[-1].T @ Bp_inf.T
    errs.append(np.sqrt(torus_integral(trapezoid((fp-fbase)**2, P, axis=1), data['dq'])))
errs = np.array(errs)
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(np.log(eps_list), np.log(errs), 1)
print(f"empirical log-log slope = {slope:.2f}  (Lipschitz: slope <= 1)")

fig, ax = paper_figure(0.5, 2.3)
ax.loglog(eps_list, errs, 'o-', ms=3.5, label=f"fitted slope ${slope:.2f}$")
ax.loglog(eps_list, np.exp(intercept)*eps_list, 'k--', lw=0.9, label="slope $1$")
ax.set_xlabel(r"$\varepsilon$")
ax.set_ylabel(r"$\|f_{W_\varepsilon}(T)-f_{W_0}(T)\|_{L^2(\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R})}$")
ax.legend()
save_figure(fig, "lipschitz")

3.4 The prior¶

In [11]:
def build_basis_cos(q, M):
    return np.stack([np.cos(m*q) for m in range(1, M+1)], axis=1)   # (Nq, M)

def make_scaling(M, tau=1.0, s=1.5):
    return np.array([tau/m**s for m in range(1, M+1)])          # prior s.d. of a_k: tau*k^(-s)

def W_from_xi(xi, Phi, scale):
    return Phi @ (scale*xi)

# truncation level K = M = 6 and s = alpha + 1 with prior regularity alpha = 1/2 (scale tau = 1)
M, tau, s = 6, 1.0, 1.5
Phi   = build_basis_cos(data['q'], M)
scale = make_scaling(M, tau, s)
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
fig, ax = paper_figure(0.65, 2.2)
for _ in range(6):
    ax.plot(q_fine, W_from_xi(rng.standard_normal(M), build_basis_cos(q_fine, M), scale),
            lw=0.9, alpha=0.85)
ax.plot(q_fine, trig_interp(data['W_true'], q_fine), 'k', lw=2, label='$W_0$')
set_q_axis(ax); ax.set_ylabel("$W(q)$"); ax.legend()
save_figure(fig, "prior_draws")

3.5 Likelihood and posterior sampling by the preconditioned Crank–Nicolson algorithm¶

One likelihood evaluation costs exactly one forward PDE solve; the posterior is sampled by the preconditioned Crank–Nicolson (pCN) algorithm in whitened coordinates.

In [12]:
B_obs = hermite_eval(inf_kw['NH'], data['p_obs'], data['beta'])   # (N_obs, NH)

def log_likelihood(W):
    _, sol = solver.solve(W, c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)     # snapshots @ dt=0.02
    pred = np.einsum('in,in->i', sol[data['t_idx'], :, data['q_idx']], B_obs)
    return -0.5*np.sum((data['Y']-pred)**2)/data['sigma']**2

W0 = W_from_xi(np.zeros(M), Phi, scale)
t0 = time.time(); ll0 = log_likelihood(W0)
print(f"one likelihood eval: {time.time()-t0:.3f}s,   ll(W=0) = {ll0:.1f}")
print(f"target plateau ~ -N_obs/2 = {-len(data['Y'])/2:.0f}")

one likelihood eval: 0.041s,   ll(W=0) = -2502.1
target plateau ~ -N_obs/2 = -1500
In [13]:
def pcn(n_iter=2500, beta_pcn=0.12, seed=1, log_every=400):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    xi = np.zeros(M); ll = log_likelihood(W_from_xi(xi, Phi, scale))
    samples = np.empty((n_iter, M)); ll_chain = np.empty(n_iter); n_acc = 0; t0 = time.time()
    for it in range(n_iter):
        eta  = rng.standard_normal(M)
        xi_p = np.sqrt(1-beta_pcn**2)*xi + beta_pcn*eta
        ll_p = log_likelihood(W_from_xi(xi_p, Phi, scale))
        if np.log(rng.random()) < ll_p - ll:
            xi, ll = xi_p, ll_p; n_acc += 1
        samples[it], ll_chain[it] = xi, ll
        if (it+1) % log_every == 0:
            print(f"  iter {it+1:5d}/{n_iter}  acc={n_acc/(it+1):6.2%}  "
                  f"ll={ll:9.1f}  elapsed={time.time()-t0:6.1f}s")
    return samples, ll_chain, n_acc/n_iter

n_iter = 2500
samples, ll_chain, acc = pcn(n_iter=n_iter, beta_pcn=0.12, seed=1)
print(f"\nFinal acceptance rate: {acc:.2%}  (target 20-50%)")

3.6 Identifiability: the Jacobian ladder and reversion to the prior¶

Linearising the forward map at the truth: the SVD of the Jacobian predicts, mode by mode, which Fourier frequencies of $W$ the data identify.

In [16]:
# Linearise the forward map at W_true and read off the identifiability structure.
xi_true = coef_true / scale          # the truth in whitened coordinates

def predict_f(xi):
    _, sol = solver.solve(W_from_xi(xi, Phi, scale), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
    return np.einsum('in,in->i', sol[data['t_idx'], :, data['q_idx']], B_obs)

h = 1e-3
F0 = predict_f(xi_true)
J = np.zeros((len(F0), M))
for m in range(M):
    e = np.zeros(M); e[m] = h
    J[:, m] = (predict_f(xi_true + e) - predict_f(xi_true - e)) / (2*h)

U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(J, full_matrices=False)
print("singular values of J   :", np.array2string(S, formatter={'float_kind':lambda v:f'{v:.2e}'}))
print("ratio to the largest    :", np.array2string(S/S[0], formatter={'float_kind':lambda v:f'{v:.1e}'}))
print("\nEach singular direction is essentially a single cosine mode:")
for j in range(M):
    dom = np.argmax(np.abs(Vt[j]))
    print(f"  sigma_{j+1} = {S[j]:.2e}   <-->   mode a_{dom+1}  (weight {Vt[j,dom]:+.2f})")

# per-mode information I_k = (sigma_k/sigma_eps)^2 of the whole data set, against the whitened
# prior precision, equal to 1 in every direction
info = (S / data['sigma'])**2
print("\ninformation I_k :", np.array2string(info, formatter={'float_kind':lambda v:f'{v:.2e}'}))
fig, ax = paper_figure(0.48, 2.1)
ax.semilogy(np.arange(1, M+1), info, 'o-', ms=3.5, label=r'$\mathscr{I}_k=(\sigma_k/\sigma_ϵ)^2$')
ax.axhline(1.0, color='C3', ls='--', lw=1, label='prior precision')
ax.set_xticks(np.arange(1, M+1)); ax.set_xlabel("mode $k$"); ax.set_ylabel("information")
ax.legend()
save_figure(fig, "info_ladder")

3.6.2 Growing the parameter dimension: the fully parametric limit¶

In [18]:
# sweep the truncation level K (= Mtry) from a few modes up to the fully parametric limit
def run_pcn_M(Mtry, n_iter=2000, beta_pcn=0.09, seed=1, s_prior=1.5, tau_prior=1.0):
    """Self-contained pCN at truncation level K = Mtry (leaves the globals of Section 3.5 untouched)."""
    Phi_M   = build_basis_cos(data['q'], Mtry)
    scale_M = make_scaling(Mtry, tau_prior, s_prior)
    def loglik(xi):
        _, sol = solver.solve(Phi_M @ (scale_M*xi), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
        pred = np.einsum('in,in->i', sol[data['t_idx'], :, data['q_idx']], B_obs)
        return -0.5*np.sum((data['Y']-pred)**2)/data['sigma']**2
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    xi = np.zeros(Mtry); ll = loglik(xi)
    samples = np.empty((n_iter, Mtry)); n_acc = 0
    for it in range(n_iter):
        xi_p = np.sqrt(1-beta_pcn**2)*xi + beta_pcn*rng.standard_normal(Mtry)
        ll_p = loglik(xi_p)
        if np.log(rng.random()) < ll_p - ll:
            xi, ll = xi_p, ll_p; n_acc += 1
        samples[it] = xi
    return dict(samples=samples, scale=scale_M, Phi=Phi_M, acc=n_acc/n_iter)

M_full = len(data['q'])//2 - 1            # every cosine mode the Nq-point grid resolves
M_grid = [3, 6, 12, M_full]
print(f"fully parametric truncation for Nq={len(data['q'])}:  K = {M_full}\n")

sweep = {}
t0 = time.time()
for Mtry in M_grid:
    res  = run_pcn_M(Mtry, n_iter=2000, beta_pcn=0.09)
    post = res['samples'][2000//5:]                     # discard first fifth as burn-in
    W_hat = res['Phi'] @ (res['scale'] * post.mean(0))
    res['post'], res['W_hat'] = post, W_hat
    res['errW'] = np.sqrt(torus_integral((W_hat - data['W_true'])**2, data['dq']))
    sweep[Mtry] = res
    print(f"  K={Mtry:2d}   acc={res['acc']:5.1%}   ||W_N - W_0||_L2 = {res['errW']:.4f}")
print(f"\nsweep wall-clock: {time.time()-t0:.0f}s")

plot_sweep(sweep, data['W_true'], 'C0', "Msweep_f")

Laplace shrinkage and posterior marginals (Section 3.6)¶

The linearisation at the truth at the fully parametric truncation $K=23$, computed here because the empirical shrinkage uses the pCN chain at $K=23$ of Section 3.6.2.

# linear-Gaussian (Laplace) posterior at the truth: which modes revert to the prior
Phi_full   = build_basis_cos(data['q'], M_full)
scale_full = make_scaling(M_full, 1.0, 1.5)
coef_true_full = cosine_coefficients(data['W_true'], data['q'], M_full)
xi_true_full   = coef_true_full / scale_full            # truth in whitened coordinates

def predict_full(xi):
    _, sol = solver.solve(Phi_full @ (scale_full*xi), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
    return np.einsum('in,in->i', sol[data['t_idx'], :, data['q_idx']], B_obs)

h  = 1e-3                                              # forward-map Jacobian by finite differences
F0 = predict_full(xi_true_full)
Jf = np.zeros((len(F0), M_full))
for m in range(M_full):
    e = np.zeros(M_full); e[m] = h
    Jf[:, m] = (predict_full(xi_true_full + e) - predict_full(xi_true_full - e)) / (2*h)

# Laplace approximation: the quadratic expansion of the log-likelihood at the truth combined with
# the N(0, I) prior on the whitened coordinates; covariance and mean in whitened coordinates
Sigma  = np.linalg.inv(np.eye(M_full) + Jf.T @ Jf / data['sigma']**2)
m_post = xi_true_full + Sigma @ (Jf.T @ (data['Y'] - F0)/data['sigma']**2 - xi_true_full)
shrink    = 1 - np.diag(Sigma)                          # posterior shrinkage S_k
prior_sd  = scale_full                                  # prior s.d. of a_k
post_sd   = scale_full * np.sqrt(np.clip(np.diag(Sigma), 0, None))   # Laplace posterior s.d. of a_k
post_mean = scale_full * m_post                         # Laplace posterior mean of a_k
coef_pcn  = sweep[M_full]['post'] * scale_full          # pCN chain at K = 23 (Section 3.6.2)

# prior against Laplace posterior marginals, mode by mode (first 12 modes)
plot_marginals(prior_sd, post_mean, post_sd, coef_true_full, shrink, name="marginals_f")

# Laplace shrinkage over all modes, with the (Monte Carlo noisy) empirical shrinkage of the chain
emp_shrink = 1 - (coef_pcn.std(0)/prior_sd)**2
modes = np.arange(1, M_full+1)
fig, ax = paper_figure(0.48, 2.1)
bars = ax.bar(modes, shrink, width=0.75, color='C0', alpha=0.75, label='Laplace')
dots, = ax.plot(modes, emp_shrink, 'o', color='C3', ms=2.8, label='pCN chain')
ax.axhline(0, color='k', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks([1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 23])
ax.set_xlabel("mode $k$"); ax.set_ylabel(r"$\mathscr{S}_k$")
ax.legend([bars, dots], ['Laplace', 'pCN chain'], loc='lower center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0),
          ncol=2, frameon=False, borderaxespad=0.2)
save_figure(fig, "shrinkage_f")

fmt = {'float_kind': lambda v: f'{v:9.2e}'}
print("k                    :", " ".join(f"{m:9d}" for m in range(1, 9)))
print("S_k (Laplace)        :", np.array2string(shrink[:8], formatter=fmt)[1:-1])
print("Laplace s.d. of a_k  :", np.array2string(post_sd[:8], formatter=fmt)[1:-1])
print("Laplace mean of a_k  :", np.array2string(post_mean[:8], formatter=fmt)[1:-1])

3.7 Density-only observations and the comparison of the two models¶

The physically natural observable is the macroscopic density $\rho_W$. Below, the inference is redone observing $\rho$ alone, and the two measurement models are compared head to head under a common noise-to-signal ratio. Setup (solver, ground truth, prior, likelihood, sampler) is re-defined self-contained for this part.

def paper_figure(frac, height, **kw):
    """Figure of width frac*TEXTWIDTH and the given height (inches), laid out at its printed size;
    the paper includes it at width frac*\\textwidth, that is, unscaled."""
    return plt.subplots(figsize=(frac*TEXTWIDTH, height), layout="constrained", **kw)

def save_figure(fig, name):
    """Write fig/<name>.pdf (vector graphics; heatmaps embedded at 600 dpi) and display it."""
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG_DIR, f"{name}.pdf"))
    plt.show()

def set_q_axis(ax, label=True):
    """Position axis on the torus T = R/2πZ ≃ [0, 2π)."""
    ax.set_xlim(0, 2*np.pi)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(5)*np.pi/2, ["$0$", r"$\pi/2$", r"$\pi$", r"$3\pi/2$", r"$2\pi$"])
    if label:
        ax.set_xlabel("$q$")

def heatmap(ax, Z, x, y, cmap, label, **kw):
    """Field Z[i, j] at the points (x[j], y[i]) of uniform grids, with a labelled colour bar."""
    dx, dy = x[1]-x[0], y[1]-y[0]
    im = ax.imshow(Z, origin='lower', aspect='auto', cmap=cmap, interpolation='bilinear',
                   extent=[x[0]-dx/2, x[-1]+dx/2, y[0]-dy/2, y[-1]+dy/2], **kw)
    cb = ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax, pad=0.02, aspect=25)
    cb.set_label(label); cb.outline.set_linewidth(0.6)
    cb.ax.tick_params(width=0.6, length=2.5)
    ax.set_ylim(y[0], y[-1])
    return im

# ---- quadrature and interpolation on the periodic grid ----------------------------------------
# On the grid q_j = j*dq of T the rectangle rule is the quadrature of the torus, exact for
# trigonometric polynomials of degree < Nq/2 (a trapezoidal rule on q_0,...,q_{Nq-1} would omit the
# closing interval [q_{Nq-1}, 2π]); momentum integrals over a finite window use the trapezoidal rule.
trapezoid = getattr(np, "trapezoid", None) or np.trapz      # np.trapz was renamed in NumPy 2.0

def torus_integral(g, dq, axis=-1):
    return np.sum(g, axis=axis)*dq

def cosine_coefficients(W, q, K):
    """Cosine coefficients a_k = (1/π) ∫_T W(q) cos(kq) dq, k = 1, ..., K, of grid values W."""
    dq = q[1] - q[0]
    a = np.array([torus_integral(W*np.cos(kk*q), dq)/np.pi for kk in range(1, K+1)])
    return np.round(a, 13) + 0.0          # rounding off the floating-point noise of exact zeros

def trig_interp(values, x, axis=-1):
    """Trigonometric interpolant of values on the grid q_j = 2πj/Nq, evaluated at the points x
    (to draw the pseudo-spectral solutions smoothly)."""
    v = np.moveaxis(np.asarray(values, dtype=float), axis, -1)
    Nq = v.shape[-1]
    E = np.exp(1j*np.outer(np.fft.fftfreq(Nq, d=1/Nq), x))
    if Nq % 2 == 0:
        E[Nq//2] = np.cos(Nq//2*x)                          # symmetric Nyquist term
    return np.moveaxis(np.real((np.fft.fft(v, axis=-1)/Nq) @ E), -1, axis)

q_fine = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 401)                       # plotting grid on [0, 2π]

# ---- plots shared by several experiments --------------------------------------------------------
def plot_reconstruction(ax, xi_samples, Phi_f, scale_, W_truth, rng_, n_draws=80, loc='upper left'):

    Phi_f is the cosine basis on q_fine and W_truth the truth on the solver grid."""

            label=r'$\widetilde{W}_N$')
    set_q_axis(ax); ax.legend(loc=loc)

def plot_coefficients(ax, mean, sd, truth, loc='best'):
    """Posterior mean ± one standard deviation of the cosine coefficients, against the truth."""
    pos = np.arange(1, len(mean)+1)
    ax.errorbar(pos, mean, yerr=sd, fmt='o', ms=3.5, capsize=2.5, elinewidth=1,
                label=r'posterior mean $\pm$ s.d.')
    ax.plot(pos, truth, 'rx', ms=6, mew=1.4, label='truth')
    ax.axhline(0, color='k', lw=0.4)
    ax.set_xticks(pos, [f"$a_{{{m}}}$" for m in pos])
    handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
    ax.legend(handles[::-1], labels[::-1], loc=loc)          # posterior first, then the truth

def plot_sweep(sweep, W_truth, color, name):
    """L^2 error of the posterior mean against the truncation level K (left) and the posterior
    means for the values of K overlaid on the truth (right)."""
    fig, ax = paper_figure(0.95, 2.2, ncols=2, gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [1, 1.6]})
    Ks = list(sweep)
    ax[0].plot(Ks, [sweep[K]['errW'] for K in Ks], 'o-', ms=3.5, color=color)
    ax[0].set_xticks(Ks); ax[0].set_ylim(bottom=0)
    ax[0].set_xlabel("truncation level $K$"); ax[0].set_ylabel(r"$\|\widetilde{W}_N-W_0\|_{L^2}$")
    for K in Ks:
        res = sweep[K]
        ax[1].plot(q_fine, build_basis_cos(q_fine, K) @ (res['scale']*res['post'].mean(0)),
                   lw=1.1, label=f"$K={K}$")
    ax[1].plot(q_fine, trig_interp(W_truth, q_fine), 'k', lw=1.8, label='$W_0$')
    set_q_axis(ax[1]); ax[1].legend(loc='upper left')

def plot_trace(ax, ll, burn, N, ylabel):
    """Log-likelihood trace with the burn-in and the plateau -N/2 marked."""
    ax.plot(ll, lw=0.5, color='C0')
    ax.axvline(burn, color='C3', ls=':', lw=1.2, label='burn-in')
    ax.axhline(-N/2, color='C2', ls='--', lw=1, label=r'$-N/2$')
    lo, hi = ll.min(), max(ll.max(), -N/2)
    pad = 0.06*(hi - lo)
    ax.set_ylim(lo - pad, hi + pad)
    ax.set_xlabel("iteration"); ax.set_ylabel(ylabel); ax.legend(loc='lower right')

def gauss(x, m, sd):
    return np.exp(-0.5*((x-m)/sd)**2)/(sd*np.sqrt(2*np.pi))

def plot_marginals(prior_sd, post_mean, post_sd, truth, shrink, label='posterior', name=None):
    """Prior (filled) against Laplace posterior marginals of a_1, ..., a_12, with the truth
    (dashed) and the posterior shrinkage S_k in each panel title."""
    fig, axes = paper_figure(0.95, 3.5, nrows=3, ncols=4)
    for m, ax in enumerate(axes.ravel()):
        lim = 3*prior_sd[m]
        xg = np.concatenate([np.linspace(-lim, lim, 801), post_mean[m] + np.linspace(-6, 6, 801)*post_sd[m]])
        xg = np.sort(xg[np.abs(xg) <= lim])
        ax.fill_between(xg, gauss(xg, 0, prior_sd[m]), color='C3', alpha=0.30, lw=0, label='prior')
        ax.plot(xg, gauss(xg, post_mean[m], post_sd[m]), color='C3', lw=1.3, label=label)
        ax.axvline(truth[m], color='k', ls='--', lw=0.9, label='truth')
        ax.set_xlim(-lim, lim); ax.set_ylim(bottom=0); ax.set_yticks([])
        ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(nbins=4, symmetric=True))
        ax.set_title(rf"$a_{{{m+1}}}$,  $\mathscr{{S}}_{{{m+1}}}={shrink[m]:.2f}$", fontsize=8)
        if m == 0:
            ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper right', handlelength=1.4)
    if name:
        save_figure(fig, name)
    else:
        plt.show()

def make_grid(Nq, L=2*np.pi):
    q = np.arange(Nq)*(L/Nq); dq = L/Nq
    k = 2*np.pi*np.fft.fftfreq(Nq, d=dq)
    return q, dq, k

def hermite_eval(NH, p, beta):
    # B[i,n] = e_n(p_i): Maxwellian-weighted Hermite functions (orthonormal, int e_n = delta_n0)
    xi = np.sqrt(beta)*np.atleast_1d(p)
    gauss = np.sqrt(beta)/np.sqrt(2*np.pi)*np.exp(-0.5*xi**2)
    B = np.zeros((len(xi), NH))
    for n in range(NH):
        c = np.zeros(n+1); c[n] = 1.0
        B[:, n] = hermeval(xi, c)/np.sqrt(float(math.factorial(n)))*gauss
    return B

def build_linear_exponentials(k, NH, gamma, beta, dt):
    # per-wavenumber exp(dt L_k) for the streaming(tridiagonal)+friction(diagonal) linear part
    Efull = np.empty((len(k), NH, NH), dtype=complex)
    n = np.arange(NH)
    for ik, kk in enumerate(k):
        L = np.zeros((NH, NH), dtype=complex)
        L[n, n] = -gamma*n
        for m in range(NH):
            if m-1 >= 0: L[m, m-1] += -(1j*kk/np.sqrt(beta))*np.sqrt(m)
            if m+1 < NH: L[m, m+1] += -(1j*kk/np.sqrt(beta))*np.sqrt(m+1)
        Efull[ik] = expm(dt*L)
    return Efull

def force_kick(c, A, tau, beta):
    # exact exponential of the nilpotent force generator (N c)_n = sqrt(beta n) A c_{n-1}
    NH = c.shape[0]; sb = np.sqrt(beta*np.arange(NH))
    out, term = c.copy(), c.copy()
    for j in range(1, NH):
        new = np.zeros_like(term)
        new[1:] = sb[1:, None]*A[None, :]*term[:-1]
        term = new*(tau/j); out += term
        if not np.any(term): break
    return out

class KineticVFP:
    def __init__(self, q, dq, k, NH, gamma, beta, dt, V):
        self.q, self.dq, self.k = q, dq, k
        self.NH, self.gamma, self.beta, self.dt = NH, gamma, beta, dt
        self.dV = np.real(np.fft.ifft(1j*k*np.fft.fft(V)))
        self.Efull = build_linear_exponentials(k, NH, gamma, beta, dt)
    def force_field(self, rho, W):
        Wconv_hat = self.dq*np.fft.fft(W)*np.fft.fft(rho)         # W*rho via FFT
        dWconv = np.real(np.fft.ifft(1j*self.k*Wconv_hat))
        return -self.dV - dWconv                                 # A = -d/dq (V + W*rho)
    def linear_step(self, c):
        chat = np.fft.fft(c, axis=1)
        chat = np.einsum('kmn,nk->mk', self.Efull, chat)
        return np.real(np.fft.ifft(chat, axis=1))
    def step(self, c, W):
        dt = self.dt
        c = force_kick(c, self.force_field(c[0], W), dt/2, self.beta)  # Strang: half kick
        c = self.linear_step(c)                                        #         full linear
        c = force_kick(c, self.force_field(c[0], W), dt/2, self.beta)  #         half kick
        return c
    def solve(self, W, c_init, Nt, save_every=1):
        c = c_init.copy(); saved, times = [c.copy()], [0.0]
        for nstep in range(Nt):
            c = self.step(c, W)
            if (nstep+1) % save_every == 0:
                saved.append(c.copy()); times.append((nstep+1)*self.dt)
        return np.array(times), np.array(saved)   # (Ns, NH, Nq)

def generate_truth(seed=0, W_true=None, Nq=48, NH_hi=20, gamma=1.0, beta=1.0, T=2.0, dt_hi=0.01):
    q, dq, k = make_grid(Nq); V = -np.cos(q)
    if W_true is None:
        W_true = -np.cos(q) + 0.5*np.cos(2*q) - 0.25*np.cos(3*q)
    rho0 = 1 + 0.6*np.sin(q) + 0.3*np.cos(2*q); rho0 = np.clip(rho0, 1e-3, None); rho0 /= rho0.sum()*dq
    c_init = np.zeros((NH_hi, Nq)); c_init[0] = rho0
    solver_hi = KineticVFP(q, dq, k, NH_hi, gamma, beta, dt_hi, V)
    times, sol = solver_hi.solve(W_true, c_init, Nt=int(T/dt_hi), save_every=2)
    return dict(q=q, dq=dq, k=k, T=T, gamma=gamma, beta=beta, V=V, rho0=rho0,
                W_true=W_true, times=times, sol_hi=sol, NH_hi=NH_hi)

def build_basis_cos(q, M): return np.stack([np.cos(m*q) for m in range(1, M+1)], axis=1)
def make_scaling(M, tau=1.0, s=1.5): return np.array([tau/m**s for m in range(1, M+1)])
def W_from_xi(xi, Phi, scale): return Phi @ (scale*xi)

M, tau, s = 6, 1.0, 1.5                 # K = 6, alpha = s - 1 = 1/2
Phi = build_basis_cos(q, M); scale = make_scaling(M, tau, s)
coef_true = cosine_coefficients(truth['W_true'], q, M)

# inference-resolution solver (coarser than the truth: NH=14, dt=0.02) and observation basis
NH_inf, dt_inf = 14, 0.02
solver = KineticVFP(q, dq, k, NH_inf, truth['gamma'], truth['beta'], dt_inf, truth['V'])
c_init_inf = np.zeros((NH_inf, len(q))); c_init_inf[0] = truth['rho0']
Nt_inf = int(truth['T']/dt_inf)
B_obs = hermite_eval(NH_inf, p_obs, truth['beta'])   # only needed for the f-likelihood

def loglik_rho(xi):
    _, sol = solver.solve(W_from_xi(xi, Phi, scale), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
    pred = sol[t_idx, 0, q_idx]                        # rho = c_0 only
    return -0.5*np.sum((Y_rho - pred)**2)/sig_rho**2

def loglik_f(xi):
    _, sol = solver.solve(W_from_xi(xi, Phi, scale), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
    pred = np.einsum('in,in->i', sol[t_idx, :, q_idx], B_obs)   # full f = sum_n c_n e_n
    return -0.5*np.sum((Y_f - pred)**2)/sig_f**2

def pcn(loglik, beta_pcn, n_iter=2500, seed=1, log_every=500):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    xi = np.zeros(M); ll = loglik(xi)
    samples = np.empty((n_iter, M)); ll_chain = np.empty(n_iter); nacc = 0; t0 = time.time()
    for it in range(n_iter):
        xp = np.sqrt(1-beta_pcn**2)*xi + beta_pcn*rng.standard_normal(M)
        lp = loglik(xp)
        if np.log(rng.random()) < lp - ll: xi, ll = xp, lp; nacc += 1
        samples[it], ll_chain[it] = xi, ll
        if (it+1) % log_every == 0:
            print(f"  iter {it+1:5d}/{n_iter}  acc={nacc/(it+1):5.1%}  ll={ll:9.1f}  t={time.time()-t0:5.0f}s")
    return samples, ll_chain, nacc/n_iter

print(f"one rho-likelihood eval costs ~", end=" ")
_t=time.time(); loglik_rho(np.zeros(M)); print(f"{time.time()-_t:.3f}s;  target plateau -N/2 = {-N_obs/2:.0f}")

one rho-likelihood eval costs ~ 0.273s;  target plateau -N/2 = -1500

Shared identifiability structure of the two observation models¶

Singular values of the forward-map Jacobian at the truth for the two models (Section 3.7.2): the two ladders have the same shape.

In [28]:
def jacobian(predict, xi0, h=1e-3):
    base = predict(xi0); J = np.zeros((len(base), M))
    for m in range(M):
        e = np.zeros(M); e[m] = h
        J[:, m] = (predict(xi0 + e) - predict(xi0 - e))/(2*h)
    return J

def predict_rho(xi):
    _, sol = solver.solve(W_from_xi(xi, Phi, scale), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
    return sol[t_idx, 0, q_idx]
def predict_f(xi):
    _, sol = solver.solve(W_from_xi(xi, Phi, scale), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
    return np.einsum('in,in->i', sol[t_idx, :, q_idx], B_obs)

xi_true = coef_true/scale
S_rho = np.linalg.svd(jacobian(predict_rho, xi_true), compute_uv=False)
S_f   = np.linalg.svd(jacobian(predict_f,   xi_true), compute_uv=False)

print("singular values of the forward-map Jacobian (whitened):")
print("  rho:", np.array2string(S_rho, formatter={'float_kind':lambda v:f'{v:.2e}'}))
print("  f  :", np.array2string(S_f,   formatter={'float_kind':lambda v:f'{v:.2e}'}))
print("\nshape (ratio to the largest) -- this is the identifiability structure:")
print("  rho:", np.array2string(S_rho/S_rho[0], formatter={'float_kind':lambda v:f'{v:.1e}'}))
print("  f  :", np.array2string(S_f/S_f[0],   formatter={'float_kind':lambda v:f'{v:.1e}'}))

3.7.3 Robustness of the density model in the fully parametric limit¶

In [29]:
# sweep the truncation level K (= Mtry) up to the fully parametric limit, from rho data
def run_pcn_M_rho(Mtry, n_iter=2000, beta_pcn=0.06, seed=1, s_prior=1.5, tau_prior=1.0):
    """Self-contained pCN on the rho-likelihood at truncation level K = Mtry."""
    Phi_M   = build_basis_cos(q, Mtry)
    scale_M = make_scaling(Mtry, tau_prior, s_prior)
    def loglik(xi):
        _, sol = solver.solve(Phi_M @ (scale_M*xi), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
        return -0.5*np.sum((Y_rho - sol[t_idx, 0, q_idx])**2)/sig_rho**2   # rho = c_0 only
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    xi = np.zeros(Mtry); ll = loglik(xi)
    samples = np.empty((n_iter, Mtry)); n_acc = 0
    for it in range(n_iter):
        xi_p = np.sqrt(1-beta_pcn**2)*xi + beta_pcn*rng.standard_normal(Mtry)
        ll_p = loglik(xi_p)
        if np.log(rng.random()) < ll_p - ll:
            xi, ll = xi_p, ll_p; n_acc += 1
        samples[it] = xi
    return dict(samples=samples, scale=scale_M, Phi=Phi_M, acc=n_acc/n_iter)

M_full = len(q)//2 - 1
M_grid = [3, 6, 12, M_full]
print(f"fully parametric truncation for Nq={len(q)}:  K = {M_full}\n")

sweep = {}
t0 = time.time()
for Mtry in M_grid:
    res  = run_pcn_M_rho(Mtry, n_iter=2000, beta_pcn=0.06)
    post = res['samples'][2000//5:]
    W_hat = res['Phi'] @ (res['scale'] * post.mean(0))
    res['post'], res['W_hat'] = post, W_hat
    res['errW'] = np.sqrt(torus_integral((W_hat - truth['W_true'])**2, dq))
    sweep[Mtry] = res
    print(f"  K={Mtry:2d}   acc={res['acc']:5.1%}   ||W_N - W_0||_L2 = {res['errW']:.4f}")
print(f"\nsweep wall-clock: {time.time()-t0:.0f}s")

plot_sweep(sweep, truth['W_true'], 'C3', "Msweep_rho")

Higher modes return to the prior, at the same rung for $\rho$ and $f$¶

Laplace shrinkage per mode for the two models at the fully parametric truncation $K=23$ (Sections 3.7.2 and 3.7.3).

In [34]:
# Laplace approximation per mode, for rho and f, at the fully parametric truncation
Phi_full   = build_basis_cos(q, M_full)
scale_full = make_scaling(M_full, 1.0, 1.5)
coef_true_full = cosine_coefficients(truth['W_true'], q, M_full)
xi_true_full = coef_true_full / scale_full

def predict_rho_full(xi):
    _, sol = solver.solve(Phi_full @ (scale_full*xi), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
    return sol[t_idx, 0, q_idx]
def predict_f_full(xi):
    _, sol = solver.solve(Phi_full @ (scale_full*xi), c_init_inf, Nt_inf, save_every=1)
    return np.einsum('in,in->i', sol[t_idx, :, q_idx], B_obs)

def laplace(predict, Y, sig):
    # shrinkage S_k, posterior s.d. and posterior mean in whitened coordinates
    h = 1e-3; F0 = predict(xi_true_full); J = np.zeros((len(F0), M_full))
    for m in range(M_full):
        e = np.zeros(M_full); e[m] = h
        J[:, m] = (predict(xi_true_full + e) - predict(xi_true_full - e)) / (2*h)
    Sig = np.linalg.inv(np.eye(M_full) + J.T @ J / sig**2)
    mean = xi_true_full + Sig @ (J.T @ (Y - F0)/sig**2 - xi_true_full)
    return 1 - np.diag(Sig), np.sqrt(np.clip(np.diag(Sig), 0, None)), mean

shrink_rho, sd_rho_w, mean_rho_w = laplace(predict_rho_full, Y_rho, sig_rho)
shrink_f,   sd_f_w,   mean_f_w   = laplace(predict_f_full,   Y_f,   sig_f)
prior_sd = scale_full

# density-only Laplace posterior against the prior, mode by mode (first 12 modes)
plot_marginals(prior_sd, scale_full*mean_rho_w, scale_full*sd_rho_w, coef_true_full, shrink_rho,
               label='posterior, model i.')

# shrinkage ladders: rho and f fall off together
modes = np.arange(1, M_full+1)
fig, ax = paper_figure(0.48, 2.1)
ax.plot(modes, shrink_rho, 'o-',  color='C3', ms=3, label='model i.')
ax.plot(modes, shrink_f,   's--', color='C0', ms=3, label='model ii.')
ax.axhline(0, color='k', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks([1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 23])
ax.set_xlabel("mode $k$"); ax.set_ylabel(r"$\mathscr{S}_k$"); ax.legend()
plt.show()
